existing_adapters.description: Tauri owns cross-platform window/tray/plugin registration; retain this path.
TokenStore and ThreadedStore provide a real provider seam.
Existing Linux/macOS/Windows RSS providers; RSS only, not all Tauri metrics.
Actual CPAL device discovery exists in GPUI; chord-voice Cpal*Buffer names alone are pure buffers, not OS capture adapters.
Linux/Android and Darwin/BSD peer credentials are implemented; Windows pipe entries are configurations only.
Native libc Unix FD transport with Linux atomic CLOEXEC and POSIX fallback already exists.
Existing Linux /proc versus non-Linux kill -0 process check; the latter is not a Windows native provider.

findings.summary: The default dependency graph and active voice plugin unconditionally require Unix file descriptors and ashpd screencast; Windows cannot type-check these APIs.
findings.minimal_strategy: Make ashpd and its session/FD ownership Linux-specific. Keep Tauri IPC registration and portable models intact; route capture through an explicit target capability/provider. Separate platform Unix transports from native credentials and portable policy modules. Do not add fake FD aliases or successful empty implementations.
targeted_checks: Record Windows x86_64/ARM64 cargo check --locked --manifest-path rust/gui-spike/Cargo.toml --all-targets errors before changes; rerun unchanged targets after each adapter slice.
Compile the real chord-client binary, not only the library; check voice IPC registrations remain present.

findings.summary: chord-platform links Secret Service/GLib and Hunspell unconditionally. libsecret has no Windows provider in the current CI setup. Tauri auth directly uses this Keyring. This is not an inherent macOS blocker: the existing macOS core job compiles with Homebrew libraries.
findings.minimal_strategy: Preserve the Keyring/TokenStore API with a real Windows credential provider; retain the working Unix libsecret implementation and its native dependency provisioning. Gate unused spellchecking/native desktop providers deliberately and verify Windows Hunspell import-library names and matching target architecture. Provision sqlite3 for chord-store too.
targeted_checks: Targeted keyring store/load/overwrite/delete/missing-entry/error-redaction contracts on native Windows with synthetic secrets.
Perform real native executable links on each OS/architecture; cargo check alone does not validate FFI libraries.

findings.summary: The active process_metrics IPC command always reads /proc/self/status. It therefore returns an error on ordinary Windows/macOS installations even if the app builds.
findings.minimal_strategy: Reuse/extract the existing GPUI native RSS adapter boundary and extend it to the complete RSS/peak/thread ProcessMetrics contract. Retain errors for unavailable or malformed measurements; never substitute zero.
targeted_checks: Test process_metrics against native OS process data for all three fields, including units and unavailable-provider errors.

findings.summary: Live audio and capture are currently Linux/PulseAudio/KWin based. Missing pactl becomes synthetic default devices, and failed KWin queries become hardcoded Orca/browser/Chord windows; these do not demonstrate native Windows/macOS support.
findings.minimal_strategy: For the requested compilation phase, isolate Linux-specific providers and document unqualified capabilities explicitly. For native functionality, extract the existing real CPAL discovery from GPUI into a shared provider and use actual native capture providers; preserve current Linux behavior and avoid invented sources or successful no-op streams.
targeted_checks: Preserve existing voice_devices/voice_stage/voice_stream contracts and numeric limits.
Add provider-unavailable cases that produce explicit capability/errors rather than fake devices/windows.
Qualify real audio/capture only on native hardware with consent; compilation is not qualification.

findings.summary: The native voice bridge is discovered under a fixed /home/sanya Discord installation and compiles a Linux C shim at runtime with gcc, GNU/POSIX headers, .so libraries and /dev/shm IPC. The configured OpenH264 asset explicitly names linux64. These are runtime/architecture assumptions, not Rust source compile errors.
findings.minimal_strategy: Keep the Linux bridge as an explicit provider with validated prerequisites and target-matched artifacts. Use standard temp/app-data paths and env::split_paths/join_paths. Do not treat a stale .node file or a missing worker as success; separate architecture-specific native qualification from the compile matrix.
targeted_checks: Unit-test provider/path selection for all six target tuples and both PATH separators.
Test missing/wrong-architecture bridge assets and failed child startup as explicit errors; do not launch live Discord during build verification.

findings.summary: SystemSources reads randomness only from /dev/urandom and ignores failure. uuid_v4 starts with a zeroed array, so the Windows default path generates constant launch/session UUIDs.
findings.minimal_strategy: Use an OS-backed randomness library/provider and propagate entropy failure instead of silently retaining zeroes. Preserve UUID version/variant formatting and injected deterministic-source contracts.
targeted_checks: Red test for unavailable/failed OS entropy; retain the existing three-UUID order and formatting tests.
Native Windows check that repeated generated identities differ and error paths never yield the all-zero-derived UUID.

findings.summary: Session/cache paths use only XDG variables or HOME. Session persistence writes plaintext token and backup files, with permission hardening compiled only for Unix; a new Windows credential adapter must not silently preserve this as its security model.
findings.minimal_strategy: Use the existing TokenStore/ThreadedStore seam for native credentials and Tauri/native application-directory resolution. Preserve legacy migration deliberately; do not rely on HOME or Unix chmod for Windows token confidentiality.
targeted_checks: Native credential persistence/restore/delete contracts with synthetic tokens and redacted errors.
Path-provider tests for absent HOME/XDG and native Windows app-data directories.

findings.summary: Current cross-platform CI has core and GPUI suites, not gui-spike. It does not explicitly build both architectures. The existing Tauri launch test treats absence of DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY as a skip on every OS, so Windows/macOS GUI testing would falsely appear headless.
findings.minimal_strategy: Add a separate six-target Tauri lane without weakening existing core/GPUI jobs. Use matching native linkers/SDKs and target-native dependency prefixes. Keep compilation/link status separate from UI/native feature qualification; make the launch environment check OS-specific before claiming native smoke coverage.
targeted_checks: cargo check/build --locked --manifest-path rust/gui-spike/Cargo.toml for each explicit target.
Targeted --lib IPC/auth/data tests and binary/plugin compilation; OS-specific offline launch smoke where a native desktop is available.
Retain all snapshot, liveness, timeout, count and payload assertions.

recommended_sequence: Add the independent six-target Tauri compile/link lane.
Fix Windows dependency and native credential/provider boundaries without changing Unix defaults.
Verify each native binary links; preserve current IPC/command interfaces and tests.
Fix OS entropy and metrics/path adapters as separate targeted red/green slices.
Document unqualified audio/capture/native bridge capabilities; qualify them separately instead of adding silent no-ops.
